newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Russian fears, poor sentiment hit De Beers.
newsitem.headline: Russian fears, poor sentiment hit De Beers.

text.p: Negative market sentiment on Thursday cut more than three percent from De Beers shares which were already undermined by anxiety over the Russian diamond deal renewal, dealers said.
By 1355 GMT De Beers had shed 425 cents to 134 rand on volume of about 295,000 shares.
Dealers said a generally poor international perception of South Africa was currently weighing on the whole market and stocks like De Beers could not escape.

They added that new worries, arising out of an accusation that Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), Russia's largest diamond producer, was guilty of financial irregularities, could delay the signing of a new marketing agreement with De Beers.
"De Beers makes up a huge component of the market and I know there have been sizeable baskets being opened. The mood is bad and De Beers is taking a blow," one dealer said.

"The guys were a bit anxious when the story about ARS came out yesterday (Wednesday). This deal has been going on for so long now. Everyone wants it out of the way," another dealer said, agreeing that the share's fall could be a delayed reaction.
Dealers said there had been sizeable selling of industrial and mining-related stock by London players.

De Beers was not seen losing any further -- good support was seen around 133-4 rand -- but dealers said the whole market would have to pick up for the share to recover, although a Russian deal might provide the necessary impetus.
